findings.where: Hero, first screen at both widths: the name block and the space beside the drawing
findings.fault: Mark is never seen. The first screen shows a drawing of the logo's arches and his name, but no photograph of him. The tile also gives no rule for how a photograph of a person would sit on the blueprint ground, so the layout round has nothing to build on.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff choosing one individual adviser, who want to see that a real, named person stands behind the advice. Mark would also object: he asked to be 'seen and heard' (client value 3). First-visit trust item 1 holds always for a solo practice.

findings.where: Hero, the line under the name: 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS', and the 'A' section bubble beside the name
findings.fault: The only words that say what Mark is share one small capitals block with drawing jargon, and they read as one label. In the 5-second look, a visitor reads him as an engineer or draughtsman, not a legal and PPP adviser.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer looking for a PPP-law adviser, who could take this for an engineering design office and leave. Mark would object too: he is selling legal judgement, not drawings.

findings.where: Hero summary: 'Advice on infrastructure projects and the laws that enable them …'
findings.fault: The line says what Mark does, but not who it is for or where he works. Development agencies, governments and the regions of his work are never named above the fold.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff, who check first whether an adviser has worked for bodies like theirs in their region. First-visit trust items 2 and 6, and 'What a visitor must be sure of' for an advisor.

findings.where: Hero summary, its closing clause 'with over 40 years of international infrastructure experience'
findings.fault: The hero's proof ends on a size word that nobody can check. The checkable fact, former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group, is not linked to anything a named body hosts. The page shows no third-party proof of any kind.
findings.who_objects: A reader who hires through procurement and judges standing by named bodies, roles and dates, not by a count of years. 'Feel the CV' bans size words, and item 14 asks for a link out to work that named bodies host when no testimonials are held.

findings.where: Hero, the 'WRITE TO MARK' button, and the title-block nav, which carries a drawing number and scale but no contact
findings.fault: The email address is never shown as text. The one action is a mailto button that hides the address. The title block, which the direction says carries the contact, gives its space to 'MMM-GA-001' and 'NTS' instead.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a work machine with no mail app set up, or one who wants to copy the address into a procurement shortlist. Neither can get the address. First-visit trust item 7 asks for the address in full as its own link text.

findings.where: Article specimen, the byline 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 • 18 September 2024'
findings.fault: The article page credits the firm, not Mark. A reader who lands on the article sees no name and no one-line bio of the person speaking in the first person.
findings.who_objects: A reader arriving from a LinkedIn post, who lands deep on the site and needs to know whose judgement this is (item 12). Mark too: the individual is the brand, never the firm's voice (client value 1).

findings.where: Article specimen, the related-item row 'Streamlining the PPP Process … Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF'
findings.fault: The lecture row leaves out its venue, which is the fact that shows who asked Mark to speak.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader, for whom 'given at a named institution' is the proof that counts. 'Feel the CV' asks for the newest talk with its venue.
